messages:
mara: Quick Q — I'm changing the payments chart to prefer an ExternalSecret lookup for STRIPE_KEY but fall back to values.stripe.key for localdeploy. Want to sanity-check the template pattern before I open a PR.

mara: Current values.yaml has:
```yaml
stripe:
  key: "local_dummy"
  useExternalSecret: false
```

mara: Proposed chart helper in _helpers.tpl:
```tpl
{{- define "payments.stripeKey" -}}
{{- if .Values.stripe.useExternalSecret }}
  {{- default (required "missing stripe secret" .Values.stripe.key) (env "STRIPE_KEY") }}
{{- else }}
  {{- .Values.stripe.key | quote }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
```

mara: then in deployment: `- name: STRIPE_KEY
  value: {{ include "payments.stripeKey" . }}`

phil: Hmm, mixing env() and ExternalSecret semantics might be confusing. If ExternalSecret writes to a k8s Secret, we should use `envFrom` or `valueFrom.secretKeyRef`. env("STRIPE_KEY") only helps for helm --set or CI.

devon: Agreed. If ExternalSecret creates secret `payments-stripe`, template should be something like:
```yaml
- name: STRIPE_KEY
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: {{ required "missing payments secret name" .Values.stripe.secretName }}
      key: stripe_key
```

jules: Also watch for rendering when `useExternalSecret=false` but secret exists in cluster — helm will still render valueFrom and the pod will pull from existing secret. That might be surprising for local tests. We sometimes use `{{- if .Values.stripe.useExternalSecret }}` guard around the whole env var.

mara: Good point. I wanted fallback so localdev works without force-creating secrets. The problem is how to conditionally produce value vs valueFrom cleanly. Any helper pattern folks prefer?

phil: I usually do a helper that returns a dict (map) and then use `toYaml`+`nindent` so you don't duplicate structure. Eg: `payments._stripeEnv` returns map {"value": ..., "valueFrom": ...} — but Helm templating with maps can be fiddly.

devon: Simpler: two partials: `payments.stripeEnvValue` (returns `value: "..."`) and `payments.stripeEnvFrom` (returns `valueFrom: ...`) and in deployment: `{{- if .Values.stripe.useExternalSecret }}{{ include "payments.stripeEnvFrom" . }}{{- else }}{{ include "payments.stripeEnvValue" . }}{{- end }}`

katie: Small ops note: if we're switching to ExternalSecret, Terraform change will add the ExternalSecret CR and a role binding for the provider. I'm going to open a PR after the helm template lands so infra can apply in one deploy. Please add the `stripe.secretName` value to the TF vars if it's new.

mara: Thanks — that's helpful. One last nuance: for chart testing (helm template CI) we don't have cluster secrets, so `required` will fail if we use it inside valueFrom. Need to avoid required on runtime secrets unless guarded by the same `if`.

jules: Exactly. Wrap `required` inside the `if .Values.stripe.useExternalSecret` block, so local templates won't break CI.

mara: Ok plan: implement two helpers (value vs valueFrom) + guard, update values with `secretName: payments-stripe`, and mark useExternalSecret default false. I'll include a note in the PR description for the TF change that infra needs to provision the ExternalSecret and provider RBAC.

phil: LGTM. @katie ping when TF PR is open so we can sequence rollout.

katie: Will do. Also adding a small docs blurb in charts/README about localdev vs cluster secret behavior.

sre-bot: Reminder: opening a change that toggles secret wiring may require a canary rollout. Consider adding `maxUnavailable: 0` during first deploy of new secret wiring. (reacted :warning:)

mara: Thanks all — I'll push a tiny PR with the helpers and example values, tag you for review.

phil: Quick nit: use `quote` on literal values to avoid YAML parsing surprises.

mara: Will do. Thanks!
